response.justification: The candidate is an experienced senior full-stack engineer (15+ years) with strong web, backend, and tooling skills, but the profile is almost entirely misaligned with this role. The position requires native-level Japanese (candidate lists English, Romanian, basic German), strong C on UNIX with Linux kernel source analysis and modification, and embedded LAN-switch security domain knowledge (MACsec, 802.1X, captive portal, L2/L3 switching, NETCONF/SNMP, chip vendor SDKs). The resume shows only brief C/C++ exposure at National Instruments (~7 months, IDE tooling) and a C++ audio thesis project, with no networking-protocol, switch firmware, or security-feature experience. Language requirement alone is likely disqualifying.
strengths: Deep, broad engineering experience across many stacks and 15+ years in industry
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, test tooling, open-source project ownership
Some low-level and systems exposure (C/C++ at National Instruments, Linux, high-performance async services)
concerns: No Japanese language ability; role requires native-level proficiency
No embedded firmware, switch/networking, or security-protocol (MACsec, 802.1X) experience
Minimal recent C/UNIX work and no evidence of Linux kernel source analysis or modification

key_factors.factor: Lack of embedded networking/security domain experience
Weak C/Linux-kernel depth despite senior general experience
